components: Methods and Techniques of the Historian
One selected 10-EC research topic; published examples vary by year and are not permanent requirements.
One permitted humanities minor; the example does not assign invented subjects.
A second permitted 15-EC humanities minor; exact field remains elective.
One year-three thematic research seminar; offered topics can change.
30EC of bachelor courses broadening study outside own programme; applicable approval and incorporation rules apply. Educational minor/exchange are separately conditioned choices.

core: Historical inquiry across ancient, medieval, early modern and contemporary periods
Critical interpretation of sources, historiography and independent research writing
Political, social, cultural, gender and religious change in history
Historical connections and globalisation as lenses for present-day questions
adjacent: Material culture, archaeology, art and heritage as evidence about the past
Modern visual and media culture and contested historical memory
questions: How do accounts of empires, war, identity and gender change with the evidence and the historian’s perspective?
How can historical research place current social and political developments in context?

trace: surveys modern political, economic and cultural developments from 1815 through the present
studies nineteenth- to twenty-first-century American lives and gender through critical storytelling
compares empires and great-power politics across world history
surveys warfare from ancient Greece and Rome to modern conflict, with historical argument about Western power
examines Indigenous American histories and cultural resistance with critical attention to excluded voices

Researching the “American Century” develops historical research questions, critical engagement with sources, methodological rigour and a substantial research paper. Currentdescription-onlyevidence supports this full research process; no Napoleonic or Walcheren outline is used.
examines traditions of political thought, contextualising how political ideals are understood across time

Comparative analysis of democratisation, institutions and political participation supplies a complementary institutional lens on changing political orders; it is not a replacement for historical period study.
analyses international relations and the historical context of geopolitics and empire
analyses theories of violent conflict and peace using historical and current cases
examines modernity, imperialism and colonial responses through social theory
traces Renaissance-to-modern art in historical contexts and introduces visual-source interpretation
uses artefacts and making practices to examine societies from prehistory through antiquity and beyond
studies African art, heritage and museum ethics, widening cultural history beyond Europe
studies cross-cultural exchange, trade and colonisation in Renaissance Mediterranean art
investigates Greek archaeology, communities and democracy as material evidence of antiquity
examines curatorial decisions and public interpretation of modern art in museums
studies the ancient Greek roots and exclusions of democracy through heritage and history
examines the history and methods of art history and how interpretations of the past change
compares ancient myths and literary traditions across world regions and historical cultural contacts
uses feminist, Marxist and minority perspectives in a research project on texts and interpretation
traces the historical evolution of cinema and its role as a cultural form
uses historical media technologies as material evidence of communication, knowledge and memory
reads twentieth- and twenty-first-century media as evidence of American social life and silenced perspectives
studies race in American history through film, photographs, music and researched narratives
traces documentary forms historically and evaluates ethical non-fiction representations

Close reading of philosophical arguments from antiquity to contemporary thought supplies complementary intellectual sources for historical interpretation of knowledge, religion, identity and ethics; it is not a philosophy-of-history specialisation.

alternatives.label: History, empire and political change
alternatives.concept: A programme in history, empire and political change, combining modern, imperial, military, gender and Indigenous histories with political thought, archaeology, art and media evidence. All six UCR History courses contribute 45 EC, including primary-source inquiry and a substantial historical research paper. Related methods and period study provide partial correspondences, while medieval survey breadth and a required 10-EC degree thesis remain different.
alternatives.labelReason: The six actual History courses anchor a sustained historical sequence; archaeology, art, media and political studies explicitly specify its material evidence and political emphasis.
progression: Every current offering and formal prerequisite checked. All selected courses have no formal prerequisites. Modern History now provides early chronological grounding; specialist historical and interpretative inquiry develops across later terms. History research and specialist300levelcourses follow earliersource/periodstudy where feasible. Year1PPD present. Open-curriculum advisory sequencing is not an additional hard prerequisite.

alternatives.label: Cultural histories and heritage
alternatives.concept: A programme in cultural histories and heritage, combining all six UCR History courses with archaeology, art and museum history, intellectual traditions, media and literary interpretation. It offers 45 EC of dedicated History alongside specialist inquiry into material, visual and textual sources. These courses support historical interpretation without reproducing Radboud’s full period-survey sequence or required 10-EC degree thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The six History courses combine with a sustained archaeology, art heritage and historical media sequence including advanced museum and historiography work.
progression: Every current offering and formal prerequisite checked. All selected courses have no formal prerequisites. Modern History now provides early chronological grounding; specialist historical and interpretative inquiry develops across later terms. History research and specialist300levelcourses follow earliersource/periodstudy where feasible. Year1PPD present. Open-curriculum advisory sequencing is not an additional hard prerequisite.
alternatives.distinctness: The programmes share20courses and differ4courses (30.0EC)each. The political route retains political thought, comparative institutions, international relations and conflict; the cultural route instead develops philosophical traditions, cinema, documentary and literary interpretation. These actual curricular priorities distinguish them; the shared African heritage course strengthens both rather than manufacturing numerical difference.

candidates.label: Secondary-school history teaching
candidates.reason: The current official History route permits an educational minor with actual school practice. UCR Youth Resilience to Extremism provides real education-related inquiry and teacher-training materials, and World Archaeology designs an educational game. These contributions do not establish a sustained programme in history pedagogy and supervised school teaching. The shortfall is academic/practical, not absence of a licence or degree title alone.

candidates.label: Historian’s independent archive and source research
candidates.reason: Historical research is already substantively represented by Researching the “American Century”, specialist source inquiry, archival work in Media & Race, and art/media historiography. A separate research-label programme would repeat these curricular priorities rather than yield a distinct24course pathway. These actual contributions do not imply a required dedicated History archive laboratory or a10ECgraduation thesis.

routeSelection.basis: Current adopted annual OER Article5 DutchGeschiedenis ordinary domestic new2026entrant pathway. Do not mix ComparativeEuropeanHistory40ECfree space or older40ECminor cohorts.

selection.assessment: Two substantive24course responses retain a common History spine while giving genuinely different political/global and cultural/material priorities. Teaching is separately assessed against actual pedagogy/school-practice content; a research-only variant duplicates existing historical/source inquiry. Stop at two.

blocks: Both survey political, economic and cultural change in modern history; UCR is weighted to1815onward.
Both examine historical connections and global power; UCR specialises in the comparative expansion, rule and legacies of empires.
No selected course establishes a dedicated medieval period survey; isolated medieval material within wider cultural or military study does not supply this component.

Both formulate historical research questions, critically investigate sources and culminate in a substantial historical paper. UCR’s7.5ECcourse is not Radboud’s required10EChistory graduation essay or a guaranteed archive-based thesis.
Both study how scholarly interpretations of the past and disciplinary methods change. UCR traces art historiography from the sixteenth century onward rather than general historical writing.

Both investigate historical evidence and the relationship between sources, knowledge and interpretation. UCR focuses on material media technologies and media-archaeological methods rather than the full historian’s toolkit.
General philosophical reading and art historiography do not establish a course centred on the philosophy of historical knowledge.
Politics, social change and historical interpretation
Both analyse gender historically using sources and contested perspectives; UCR concentrates on North America from the nineteenth century onward.

Both develop focused historical inquiry and source-based interpretation. UCR studies Indigenous histories, colonial institutions and marginalized voices; the relationship concerns historical research, not equivalence to every topic in Radboud’s changing seminar offer.

Archival inquiry into photographs, news, film and other records contributes directly to historical source research. UCR integrates this with racial and cultural history, participant observation and public media, rather than a dedicated general archive laboratory.
No selected course centres on historical relationships between human societies and the environment.
Personal development and public-history projects do not establish this History-specific career-orientation course.
Historical visions of the future and public interpretation are present in selected courses, but do not establish the dedicated reflection on historians’ present and future professional role.
Cultural history, material evidence and open study

Renaissance Mediterranean art, trade, colonisation and cross-cultural exchange address a substantive part of early modern cultural history. UCR uses artistic evidence rather than the full period survey.

Both develop a focused historical research question and an independently researched argument. UCR specialises in modern art and museum histories; Radboud’s restricted seminar topics vary and topic equivalence is not asserted.
Athenian democracy, social divisions, religion, primary texts and material evidence address an identifiable part of ancient history. UCR does not reproduce the full ancient-world survey.
This is a restricted15ECArtsminor package, not a predetermined subject that one selected UCR course can replace.
This is a second restricted15ECArtsminor package; package integrity and permitted choices remain distinct from single-course comparison.
Genuine30ECopenstudy outside the own programme has no fixed substantive counterpart.

notes.text: UCR combines dedicated History with archaeology, art, media, intellectual traditions and political inquiry. These courses provide substantive but partial historical and research correspondences. Radboud offers a fuller period-survey sequence, dedicated History methods and historiography, fixed minor packages and a required 10-EC historical graduation essay; shared rows do not imply equivalent disciplinary coverage.

audience.programmeDescription: History examines change from antiquity to the present and how historians construct accounts of the past. This comparison follows the Dutch-language History pathway in the adopted 2026–2027 regulations.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Both UCR programmes include all six History courses, totalling 45 EC. One emphasises empire and political change; the other cultural history and heritage. Archaeology, art, media and textual inquiry contribute specific historical sources and methods. Shared rows indicate partial relationships, including archival inquiry, art historiography and a substantial historical research paper. UCR does not reproduce Radboud’s full chronological survey sequence or its required 10-EC degree thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The pathway contains 60 EC in each year: 100 EC of compulsory courses, 20 EC of restricted thematic seminars, 30 EC of fixed Arts minor packages and 30 EC of open bachelor study outside the own programme. Mentorship, academic language assessment and personal/professional development include additional noncredit requirements. The ordinary first-year study-advice threshold is 45 EC.
